newsitem.title: FRANCE: Huge blast rocks central Algiers - residents.
newsitem.headline: Huge blast rocks central Algiers - residents.

text.p: A huge blast rocked central Algiers on Tuesday afternoon, residents said.

"We heard a strong explosion just a few minutes ago and people believed the blast might have occurred near Champ des Manoeuvres neighbourhood," said one resident, speaking by telephone from the city which has suffered numerous bomb attacks blamed by the authorities on Moslem fundamentalists.
Residents said later they believed the blast was a car bomb near the main university faculty in central Algiers.

One quoted a taxi driver who said he witnessed the blast as saying it was in the main shopping street, Rue Didouche Mourad. First reports suggested the blast was in Champs des Manoeuvres Square, some 300 metres (yards) from the street.
There was no official report or comment immediately from the authorities. Two car bombs in Algiers late in December killed at least 18 people.

About 60,000 people have died, including more than 1,400 in bomb attacks, in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
